redstone_help.heading: Redstone Block Description
redstone_help.redstone.summary: Carries redstone signals when placed on blocks.
redstone_help.redstone.detail1: Signal strength ranges from 0 to 15 and drops by 1 for each dust step.
redstone_help.redstone_torch.summary: Normally on; switches off when the block it is attached to is powered.
redstone_help.redstone_torch.detail2: Repeatedly switching off in a short time can burn it out temporarily.
redstone_help.redstone_block.summary: A constant power source that outputs strength 15.
redstone_help.redstone_block.detail1: Cannot be switched off by a signal, but can be moved by pistons.
redstone_help.repeater.summary: Sends a rear input forwards and restores its strength to 15.
redstone_help.repeater.detail1: Right-clicking sets a delay of 1–4 redstone ticks: 0.1–0.4 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.repeater.detail2: A powered repeater or comparator pointing into its side locks its current output state.
redstone_help.comparator.summary: Compares rear and side signal strengths, or reads how full a container is.
redstone_help.comparator.detail1: Compare mode: passes the rear signal if it is at least as strong as the strongest side input.
redstone_help.comparator.detail2: Subtract mode: outputs the rear input minus the strongest side input, with a minimum of 0.
redstone_help.comparator.detail3: Right-clicking changes modes. The small front torch is lit in subtract mode.
redstone_help.observer.summary: Detects block state changes at its face and sends a short pulse from its back.
redstone_help.observer.detail1: The red dot outputs strength 15 for 1 redstone tick.
redstone_help.observer.detail2: Detects changes such as crop growth and piston movement, but not every change to a block's internal data.
redstone_help.lever.summary: A manual switch that toggles on and off when right-clicked.
redstone_help.lever.detail1: Outputs strength 15 continuously while switched on.
redstone_help.lever.detail2: Does not turn off automatically. Its on or off state remains until toggled again.
redstone_help.stone_button.summary: Outputs a brief strength-15 signal when pressed.
redstone_help.stone_button.detail1: Turns off after 1 second at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.stone_button.detail2: Unlike wooden buttons, it cannot be pressed by arrows.
redstone_help.wood_button.summary: Outputs strength 15 when pressed by hand or hit by an arrow.
redstone_help.wood_button.detail1: A manual press lasts 1.5 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.wood_button.detail2: It stays powered while an arrow remains in contact with the button.
redstone_help.stone_pressure_plate.summa: Outputs strength 15 when a player or mob stands on it.
redstone_help.stone_pressure_plate.detai: Dropped items alone do not activate it.
redstone_help.wood_pressure_plate.summar: Detects players, mobs, dropped items and other entities resting on it.
redstone_help.wood_pressure_plate.detail: Outputs strength 15 regardless of the number of detected entities.
A single dropped item activates it.
redstone_help.light_weighted_pressure_pl: A gold pressure plate whose signal increases with the number of entities on it.
Adds 1 signal strength per entity, up to 15 at 15 or more entities.
A merged stack of dropped items counts as one entity, not as each individual item.
redstone_help.heavy_weighted_pressure_pl: An iron pressure plate for measuring larger numbers of entities.
1–10 entities give strength 1, 11–20 give 2, and 141 or more give the maximum 15.
A merged stack of dropped items counts as one entity.
redstone_help.daylight_detector.summary: Outputs a redstone signal based on sunlight.
redstone_help.daylight_detector.detail1: Signal strength changes with time, weather and sky light.
redstone_help.daylight_detector.detail2: Right-clicking switches between normal and inverted modes.
redstone_help.target.summary: Outputs a signal based on where a projectile hits it.
redstone_help.target.detail1: Hits closer to the center produce stronger signals, up to strength 15.
redstone_help.target.detail2: Adjacent redstone dust connects towards the target block.
redstone_help.tripwire_hook.summary: Two facing hooks connected by string detect entities crossing the line.
redstone_help.tripwire_hook.detail1: An attached tripwire outputs strength 15 when an entity touches the string.
redstone_help.tripwire_hook.detail2: Cutting connected string with shears does not trigger the hooks.
redstone_help.string.summary: Placed string forms tripwire that detects entities.
redstone_help.string.detail1: A continuous line of string connects two tripwire hooks facing each other.
redstone_help.string.detail2: Entities touching the connected string make the hooks output a redstone signal.
redstone_help.sculk_sensor.summary: Detects nearby vibrations such as footsteps and block placement.
redstone_help.sculk_sensor.detail1: Output strength depends on the distance to the vibration source.
redstone_help.sculk_sensor.detail2: A comparator reads the vibration frequency. Wool blocks vibration transmission.
redstone_help.calibrated_sculk_sensor.su: A side input selects the vibration frequency this sensor detects.
redstone_help.calibrated_sculk_sensor.de: An input of strength 1–15 at the amethyst face limits detection to that frequency.
Input 0 accepts all frequencies. It has a longer detection range than a regular sculk sensor.
redstone_help.piston.summary: Extends when powered to push blocks in front of it.
redstone_help.piston.detail1: Moves up to 12 blocks at once. Some blocks, such as obsidian, cannot be pushed.
redstone_help.piston.detail2: Only the arm returns when power is removed. It does not pull the front block back.
redstone_help.sticky_piston.summary: Pushes blocks and can pull the front block back when retracting.
redstone_help.sticky_piston.detail1: Moves up to 12 blocks, including blocks carried by attached slime or honey blocks.
redstone_help.sticky_piston.detail2: In Java Edition, a very short pulse can cause it to retract without pulling the front block back.
redstone_help.slime_block.summary: Carries attached neighboring blocks when moved by a piston.
redstone_help.slime_block.detail1: Attached blocks count towards the piston's 12-block movement limit.
redstone_help.slime_block.detail2: Does not stick to honey blocks.
redstone_help.honey_block.summary: A sticky block that carries neighboring blocks when moved by a piston.
redstone_help.honey_block.detail1: Does not stick to slime blocks. Attached blocks still count towards the movement limit.
redstone_help.honey_block.detail2: It does not conduct redstone power.
redstone_help.dispenser.summary: Uses or fires one stored item whenever it receives a new power signal.
redstone_help.dispenser.detail1: Behavior depends on the item: shoots arrows, uses water buckets, applies bone meal and more.
redstone_help.dispenser.detail2: Constant power does not activate it repeatedly. It activates again when power turns off and then on.
redstone_help.dropper.summary: Sends one stored item forwards each time it receives a new power signal.
redstone_help.dropper.detail1: Inserts into a container in front of it, or drops an item if there is no container.
redstone_help.dropper.detail2: Does not execute the functions of arrows or buckets. It activates again when power turns off and then on.
redstone_help.hopper.summary: Collects items from above and transfers them into the container its spout points toward.
redstone_help.hopper.detail1: Redstone power locks its own pulling and pushing of items.
redstone_help.hopper.detail2: Other hoppers can still insert into a locked hopper. A comparator can read its fullness.
redstone_help.crafter.summary: Crafts the arranged recipe when it receives a new redstone signal.
redstone_help.crafter.detail1: Clicking an empty slot toggles its enabled state. Disabled slots do not accept ingredients.
redstone_help.crafter.detail2: A comparator counts occupied or disabled slots, giving a signal from 0 to 9.
redstone_help.redstone_lamp.summary: A lamp that lights up when powered by redstone.
redstone_help.redstone_lamp.detail1: Emits light level 15 while on. Turns off after a short delay when power is removed.
redstone_help.copper_bulb.summary: Toggles between lit and unlit each time it receives a new power signal.
redstone_help.copper_bulb.detail1: It keeps its on/off state when power is removed and changes state at the next rising signal.
redstone_help.copper_bulb.detail2: A comparator reads strength 15 while it is lit. Oxidation reduces its light level.
redstone_help.note_block.summary: Plays its configured note when it receives a new power signal.
redstone_help.note_block.detail1: Right-clicking changes pitch. The block underneath changes the instrument.
redstone_help.note_block.detail2: Regular instruments require air directly above. A mob head on top plays that mob's sound instead.
redstone_help.tnt.summary: Redstone power primes it to explode after a short fuse.
redstone_help.tnt.detail1: An ordinary redstone activation gives a fuse of about 4 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.tnt.detail2: Removing power does not cancel primed TNT.
redstone_help.rail.detail1: Redstone can switch the direction of a curved rail at a junction.
redstone_help.rail.detail2: Regular rails have no mechanism to accelerate carts.
redstone_help.powered_rail.summary: Accelerates minecarts when powered and brakes them when unpowered.
redstone_help.powered_rail.detail1: A directly powered rail also activates connected powered rails.
redstone_help.powered_rail.detail2: Starting a stationary cart depends on track layout, such as a slope or a blocked end.
redstone_help.detector_rail.summary: Outputs strength 15 while a minecart is on it.
redstone_help.detector_rail.detail1: A comparator reads the fullness of a chest or hopper minecart on the rail.
redstone_help.activator_rail.summary: When powered, triggers special functions of passing minecarts.
redstone_help.activator_rail.detail1: Can eject passengers or prime TNT minecarts.
redstone_help.activator_rail.detail2: Also controls hopper minecart collection. Does not accelerate minecarts.
redstone_help.iron_door.summary: An iron door opened and closed by redstone power.
redstone_help.iron_door.detail2: Opens when powered and closes when power is removed.
redstone_help.iron_trapdoor.summary: An iron trapdoor opened and closed by redstone power.
redstone_help.iron_trapdoor.detail2: Opens when powered and closes when power is removed.
redstone_help.door.summary: A door you can open by hand or control with redstone.
redstone_help.door.detail1: A change to powered opens it; a change to unpowered closes it.
redstone_help.trapdoor.summary: A trapdoor you can operate by hand or with redstone.
redstone_help.trapdoor.detail1: A change to powered opens it; a change to unpowered closes it.
redstone_help.fence_gate.summary: A fence gate you can operate by hand or with redstone.
redstone_help.fence_gate.detail1: A change to powered opens it; a change to unpowered closes it.
redstone_help.fence_gate.detail2: Blocks passage like a fence when closed.
redstone_help.trapped_chest.summary: Outputs a redstone signal while players have it open.
redstone_help.trapped_chest.detail1: Signal strength equals the number of players viewing it, up to 15.
redstone_help.trapped_chest.detail2: A comparator reads stored-item fullness, rather than the number of viewers.
redstone_help.container.summary: A comparator can read how full this container is.
redstone_help.container.detail1: A comparator reads the container when its rear faces it. Empty gives 0; completely full gives 15.
redstone_help.container.detail2: The signal accounts for slot count and item stack limits, not just the total number of items.
redstone_help.lectern.summary: Produces a short redstone pulse when a book page is turned.
redstone_help.lectern.detail1: A comparator reads the current page position as a strength from 1 to 15.
redstone_help.lectern.detail2: With no book, comparator output is 0.
redstone_help.composter.summary: A comparator can read its composting stage.
redstone_help.composter.detail1: Empty gives 0, rising with each stage to 8 when ready to harvest.
redstone_help.composter.detail2: A hopper above can add compostable items; a hopper below can extract finished bone meal.
redstone_help.lightning_rod.summary: Briefly outputs strength 15 when struck by lightning.
redstone_help.lightning_rod.detail1: Requires an actual lightning strike. Rain alone does not activate it.
redstone_help.jukebox.summary: Outputs redstone while playing music; a comparator identifies the stored disc.
redstone_help.jukebox.detail1: Outputs strength 15 while a disc is playing.
redstone_help.jukebox.detail2: Comparator strength depends on the type of disc inside.
redstone_help.image.bulb_memory: Stays lit after power is removed
redstone_help.image.rail_empty: Detector rail · no cart · output off
redstone_help.image.rail_cart: Detector rail · cart detected · output on
redstone_help.extra.powered_rail.1: Power travels through up to 8 connected powered rails in each direction from a directly powered rail.
redstone_help.extra.powered_rail.2: On a straight line with direct power supplied only to the center rail, 8 rails on each side plus the center gives 17 powered rails. The ninth rail on either side needs another power source.
redstone_help.extra.powered_rail.3: Distance counts connected rails, including slopes. A normal, detector or activator rail interrupts propagation through powered rails.
redstone_help.extra.powered_rail.4: An activated powered rail does not output power to neighboring redstone dust.
redstone_help.extra.activator_rail.1: Power propagates through up to 8 connected activator rails in each direction from a directly powered one.
redstone_help.extra.activator_rail.2: Powered rails and activator rails do not pass activation between the two types. Activator rails do not accelerate minecarts.
redstone_help.extra.note_block.1: Each right-click raises the pitch by one semitone, cycling through 25 pitches over two octaves. The actual register depends on the instrument.
redstone_help.extra.note_block.2: It plays once when power changes from off to on. Continuous power does not repeat the note.
redstone_help.extra.note_block.3: Block underneath → instrument (representative materials). A mob head above takes priority over the block below.
redstone_help.extra.note_block.4: Dirt, grass block and other default materials → harp / piano
redstone_help.extra.note_block.5: Stone, cobblestone and similar materials → bass drum
redstone_help.extra.note_block.6: Sand, gravel, concrete powder → snare drum
redstone_help.extra.note_block.7: Glass, sea lantern and similar materials → hi-hat / clicks
redstone_help.extra.note_block.8: Wood planks, logs and similar materials → bass
redstone_help.extra.note_block.24: Waxed copper blocks use the same sound as their matching oxidation stage. The copper entries above refer to full copper blocks.
redstone_help.extra.note_block.25: Heads placed on top: zombie, skeleton, wither skeleton, creeper, dragon and piglin. These sounds are not pitch-tuned. A player head can use a separately configured custom sound.
redstone_help.extra.repeater.1: Any input from 1 to 15 produces output 15. An input of 0 produces 0.
redstone_help.extra.repeater.2: Locking holds either the on or off state. The side locking signal must end before the repeater responds to its rear input again.
redstone_help.extra.comparator.1: Rear input 10 and side input 7 gives output 10 in compare mode and 3 in subtract mode.
redstone_help.extra.comparator.2: Rear input 7 and side input 10 gives 0 in both modes. When both sides have input, the stronger side is used.
redstone_help.extra.comparator.3: It can also read values such as container fullness, book pages or disc type. The meaning depends on the block behind it.
redstone_help.extra.hopper.1: It has 5 slots. It pulls from a container above and pushes into the container at its output.
redstone_help.extra.hopper.2: Ordinary container transfers move 1 item every 8 game ticks: 2.5 items per second at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.extra.hopper.3: Picking up a dropped stack differs from transferring single items between containers. Multiple items from the stack can be collected together when space is available.
redstone_help.extra.piston.1: In Java Edition, pistons cannot move blocks with block entities, such as chests, barrels, furnaces or hoppers.
redstone_help.extra.piston.2: It cannot extend if an immovable block obstructs the push or if more than 12 blocks would need to move.
redstone_help.extra.sticky_piston.1: It shares the normal piston's movement limits. In Java it cannot move block entities such as chests, barrels, furnaces or hoppers.
redstone_help.extra.sticky_piston.2: On retraction it pulls the movable block immediately in front of the head. Blocks attached through slime or honey also count toward the movement limit.
redstone_help.extra.sticky_piston.3: A 1-redstone-tick pulse in Java can push a block out without pulling it back.
redstone_help.extra.sculk_sensor.1: Its vibration detection radius is 8 blocks. A vibration takes time to travel from its source to the sensor.
redstone_help.extra.sculk_sensor.2: It is active for 30 game ticks, followed by a 10-game-tick cooldown: 1.5 and 0.5 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.extra.sculk_sensor.3: Its ordinary output strength depends on distance; its comparator frequency identifies the vibration type. These are different values.
redstone_help.extra.calibrated_sculk_sen: Its detection radius is 16 blocks, compared with 8 for a normal sculk sensor.
It is active for 10 game ticks and then cools down for 10 game ticks: 0.5 seconds each at the default tick rate.
The strength supplied to the amethyst input side selects a vibration frequency. It does not fix the output strength to that value.
redstone_help.extra.crafter.1: It uses a 3×3 crafting grid. Disabled slots count as empty for recipes and reject incoming ingredients.
redstone_help.extra.crafter.2: The result is ejected from the front or transferred into a container there when it can accept the item.
redstone_help.extra.copper_bulb.1: Light levels by oxidation stage: copper 15, exposed 12, weathered 8, oxidized 4.
redstone_help.extra.copper_bulb.2: A lit bulb gives comparator output 15 regardless of oxidation. Light level and redstone signal strength are different values.
redstone_help.extra.container.1: An ordinary empty container outputs 0. Otherwise its output is 1 plus the rounded-down value of 14 times the average slot fullness.
redstone_help.extra.container.2: A slot's fullness uses that item's maximum stack size. A tool that stacks to 1 and a block that stacks to 64 fill different fractions even with the same item count.
redstone_help.extra.container.3: Example: a 27-slot chest containing one full stack of a 64-stack item outputs 1. Filling all 27 slots with full stacks gives 15.
redstone_help.extra.detector_rail.1: A minecart on the rail powers connected dust at strength 15. The signal turns off after the cart leaves.
redstone_help.extra.detector_rail.2: It detects ordinary minecarts too. Comparator output for a minecart's inventory is separate from its detection signal.
